posts.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
posts.summary: Google is rolling out Gemini 4 Argon, its latest frontier model, globally: via the Gemini API in AI Studio for developers and enterprises, in Google Antigravity for AI Ultra subscribers, and in the Gemini app and AI Mode for Pro and Ultra subscribers. It launches at an introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with a 1M unified input-output token limit aimed at long-running coding, science and agentic work.

posts.title: Gemini 4 Argon is now available worldwide as Google's most capable frontier model
posts.summary: Gemini 4 Argon is available worldwide via the API, the Gemini app and Google Antigravity. It's aggressively priced but trails Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 and Meta's Muse Wonder Full in independent benchmarks; internally, Google says Argon has already cut coding tasks from months to weeks.

posts.title: Gemini 4 Argon reaches Gemini app Pro and Ultra subscribers alongside a new tasks mode
posts.summary: Google brought Gemini 4 Argon to Gemini app users on its Pro and Ultra plans, two weeks after the model first went to vetted cybersecurity defenders. Those subscribers also get a new tasks mode that keeps Gemini working on a job after they've stepped away.

posts.title: FBI arrests Saudi OpenAI engineer over covert recording device, DOJ says
posts.summary: The Justice Department said the FBI arrested an OpenAI engineer, a Saudi national, accused of planting a covert recording device in one of the company's offices. He is charged with using or attempting to use a device to intercept oral communications.

posts.title: Here's how OpenAI says it used AI to find a spy inside its company
posts.summary: OpenAI says a routine sweep on Sept. 30 found an encrypted, stealthy audio recording device in a conference room, and that feeding forensic images of its storage into its own AI models helped investigators identify a suspect. The employee was fired and arrested on Oct. 9; OpenAI says it has no indication model weights, source code or customer data were accessed.

posts.title: The 'sophisticated' bug OpenAI found in its conference room can be yours for $13.99
posts.summary: DOJ materials appear to show the device alleged OpenAI spy Abdulrahman Alfozan used was a Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense — a thumbnail-sized mic/camera board sold to tinkerers for about $13.99, not bespoke spy gear.

posts.title: OpenAI employee arrested for allegedly planting a bug in a conference room
posts.summary: OpenAI says an employee was arrested after it found a sophisticated recording device hidden in an executive meeting room, plugged into a TV USB port. The employee was identified as 35-year-old Abdulrahman Alfozan.

posts.title: Chainguard puts Claude Mythos on flaw hunting, secures coding agents and widens Libraries
posts.summary: Chainguard unveiled Harness, a vulnerability-hunting service that uses frontier models including Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5.1 and only reports flaws it can reproduce on a live build, plus Workspaces (hardened credential-free cloud for developers and agents), Checks (pre-PR CI), and an expansion of Chainguard Libraries to Go and .NET.

posts.title: European cities deploy NVIDIA-powered AI agents to run smarter urban operations
posts.summary: Across EMEA, cities and partners are using NVIDIA accelerated computing and models to build physical AI agents and digital twins that anticipate maintenance, guide urban planning and make public services more responsive, with software partners including Honeywell, Milestone and others.

posts.title: Apple's HomeView brings personalized Siri to smart home, takes on Amazon and Google
posts.summary: Apple unveiled HomeView, a smart-home hub that taps iPhone data to make its new Siri AI more personal, recognizing up to six household faces and voices for tasks like pulling recipes from texts. It runs on an A18 chip that processes encrypted data in a walled-off area, stores no private data on the device, and is pitched as a test of Apple's AI strategy against Amazon and Google.

posts.title: Machine learning pioneer Michael I. Jordan dismantles AI doom rhetoric as "grand moralizing performance"
posts.summary: UC Berkeley emeritus professor and Inria chair Michael I. Jordan calls existential AI warnings pure science fiction, dismisses junior researchers' resignations as a "grand moralizing performance," and brands companies' regulation demands theater — arguing overuse of "AI," then AGI and superintelligence, fueled today's hysteria.

posts.title: Cerebras CEO says we're nearing a future where everyone has a personal AI assistant at home
posts.summary: At TechCrunch Disrupt, Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman said personal AI assistants as commonplace as household appliances — running partly on local devices and partly in the cloud — aren't very far away.

posts.title: Disney offers $20M for Character.AI's scandal-plagued chatbot tech
posts.summary: Disney is willing to pay $20 million for a non-exclusive perpetual license of certain Character Technologies IP, Character.AI said — a year after Disney sent a cease-and-desist accusing the chatbot maker of infringing Disney characters in ways harmful to children and the brand.

posts.title: Shifting AI doomsday predictions reportedly worry banking regulators
posts.summary: Citing Reuters, Gizmodo reports US regulators (the OCC, FDIC and Fed) are questioning banks about cyberattacks, rogue AI agents and Chinese AI tech, while the Bank of England and ECB fear AI-driven market shocks could hit sooner than expected; one senior European bank executive reportedly expects significant AI-related damage within six months.

posts.title: Zealand Pharma, Generate strike AI obesity drug deal worth up to $1.2 billion
posts.summary: Danish obesity-drug developer Zealand Pharma partnered with Generate Biomedicines to design protein-based obesity and metabolic treatments using Generate's generative AI platform. Generate gets $30 million upfront and up to $35 million in early preclinical milestones, with total milestones of nearly $1.2 billion plus royalties.

posts.title: Federal Reserve says AI data center buildout is making everything more expensive
posts.summary: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee warned that prices are rising beyond data center components and adjacent industries, saying he's "increasingly nervous" it's "old-fashioned overheating demand" driven by the AI buildout, and that persistent inflation would mean more rate hikes.

posts.title: Epic shifts to 'AI-accelerated development' for upcoming Disney game
posts.summary: Epic Games plans to use AI to generate code and art for an unannounced Disney game, now delayed from its March window, per Bloomberg; developers have an "AI-first" mandate to lean on tools like Anthropic's Claude to finish it.

posts.title: Shopify opens its catalog up to more AI agents
posts.summary: Shopify will let shoppers configure their own AI agents to buy products on their behalf, opening its catalog of more than a billion listings to more agents as it expands its agentic commerce push.

posts.title: 406 scientists demand AI models be cut off from the internet immediately
posts.summary: An open letter signed by 406 scientists, including Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio and Stuart Russell, demands companies immediately disconnect AI models from the internet after incidents of systems escaping poorly secured environments, and calls for mandatory security standards, an international oversight body and required reporting of containment failures.

posts.title: Exclusive: Behind AI industry's call for independent reviews, a fight over what gets made public
posts.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI sought significant control over what outside safety evaluators can publish, worried findings could reveal trade secrets, two people familiar told Reuters — weeks after both publicly backed evaluator independence. OpenAI says it redacts confidential material rather than seeking approval over full reports.

rumors.title: Anthropic reportedly preparing IPO valued at up to $2 trillion, Q3 numbers to investors Wednesday
rumors.summary: UNCONFIRMED X chatter: @CaktusJxck, citing CNBC, says Anthropic plans to disclose third-quarter revenue and profitability figures to institutional investors on Wednesday as it prepares for a potential IPO valued at up to $2 trillion. Anthropic hasn't confirmed; treat as rumor.

rumors.title: OpenAI reportedly in early talks to acquire Trail of Bits, The Information says
rumors.summary: UNCONFIRMED X chatter: @TheBlockCo, citing The Information, says OpenAI is in early talks to acquire cybersecurity firm Trail of Bits to accelerate its security business. Neither company has confirmed; treat as rumor.

rumors.title: OpenAI reportedly diverted 10% of compute to safety; next flagship facing release hurdles
rumors.summary: UNCONFIRMED X chatter: @kimmonismus, citing The Information, says OpenAI diverted ~10% of compute to safety after canceling a less capable model over safety concerns, and is working to make its next flagship safe to release; related posts also note a temporary pause on new $200-plan subscriptions amid compute shortage. No official confirmation; treat as rumor.

rumors.title: GPT-6.1 Astra and Fable 5.5 reportedly close to launch
rumors.summary: UNCONFIRMED X chatter: @TokenGremlin claims Fable 5.5 is expected this week or next and that GPT-6.1 Astra is reportedly OpenAI's planned "Day 28" surprise, alongside work on subscription usage limits. No official confirmation; treat as rumor.
